cmad.notes: No Parker Solar Probe CMAD located after all three search strategies. (a) Designated repository: a Zenodo full-text query for "Parker Solar Probe" CMAD returned 244 hits, none of which is a Calibration and Measurement Algorithms Document (all are science datasets, catalogues, software and conference material). (b) Data-centre sites: the SPDF/CDAWeb PSP readme (https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/sp_phys/data/psp/00readme.html, last updated 2022-02-16) describes each suite and names its PI but links no CMAD; the APL PSP Science Gateway (https://sppgway.jhuapl.edu/) is a JavaScript application with no crawlable document index, so it could not be inspected without a browser. (c) General web search surfaced CMADs for other heliophysics missions (MMS, SDO/EVE, STEREO/SWAVES, SABER) and the 2023 Heliophysics Senior Review report (which confirms CMADs are a standing requirement), but no PSP document. Parker Solar Probe is still operating (no StopDate; perihelia scheduled through 2026) and is NASA-funded under Living With a Star contract NNN06AA01C, so a CMAD is expected to exist and its absence from public locations is a notable gap - it may be held internally at APL or GSFC. Current-team evidence was instead taken from the JHU/APL mission team page, which is dated 2026 and names the sitting instrument PIs.

instrument_coverage.notes: The external roster is unambiguous and every source agrees: Parker Solar Probe carries exactly four science instrument suites - FIELDS, WISPR, SWEAP and IS⊙IS. This is stated by the NASA Science mission page, the NASA Science instruments page (which also names a PI for each suite), the JHU/APL mission team page (which lists four 'Instrument Principal Investigators'), the SPDF/CDAWeb PSP readme (four data subdirectories plus ephemeris), the mission overview paper (Fox et al. 2015, 10.1007/s11214-015-0211-6), and the processed record's own Description. All four have SPASE Instrument records, so nothing is missing from SPASE at suite level. Two structural gaps exist one level down and are worth flagging to curators rather than counted as missing instruments: (1) IS⊙IS/EPI-Hi has no Instrument record of its own - only its three telescopes (HET, LET1, LET2) are registered, under an EPI-Hi directory that contains no EPI-Hi record; (2) FIELDS/RFS (the Radio Frequency Spectrometer) likewise has no record of its own, only its HFR and LFR receivers. A third oddity: the FIELDS Time Domain Sampler is registered at the path FIELDS/FIELDS2/TDS, where the intermediate 'FIELDS2' directory has no record and appears to be a pathing artefact rather than a real instrument. The clone was verified against the published registry at spase-metadata.org and the two agree exactly on all 25 records above. The Ephemeris record is a housekeeping/trajectory pseudo-instrument, not a payload element, and carries only metadata contacts.

pending_instrument_runs.notes: This Observatory run resolved FIELDS at suite level only (Contacts PI plus positions 1-3 of the suite paper). Each sub-instrument has its own SPASE record, but all eleven carry identical Contacts - Stuart D. Bale as PrincipalInvestigator, Nicola J. Fox as ProjectScientist, Lee Frost Bargatze as MetadataContact - so no new people are recoverable from the records themselves. The sub-instrument leads (for example the MAG fluxgate, SCM search coil, Digital Fields Board and Radio Frequency Spectrometer teams) are described in dedicated sections of the suite paper (Bale et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-016-0244-5) and in separate sub-instrument papers, none of which were resolved here. A per-instrument finder pass is needed for each.

A trajectory/housekeeping pseudo-instrument rather than a payload element. Its Contacts list only James M. Weygand and Lee Frost Bargatze as MetadataContacts, so it yields no author candidates, and it has no description paper of its own - its InformationURLs point at the mission overview paper and the NSSDC spacecraft entry. The people behind PSP ephemeris production are the APL mission design and navigation team (see the excluded mission-team entries below); a dedicated pass would need the SPICE kernel documentation at https://spdf.gsfc.nasa.gov/pub/data/psp/ephemeris/.

notes: Paper selection confident for the Observatory description paper. (Fox et al. 2015, 10.1007/s11214-015-0211-6), 'The Solar Probe Plus Mission: Humanity's First Visit to Our Star', passes every heuristic: mission-overview title keywords, 14 authors, 1234 Crossref citations, publication in November 2015 - within the fuzzy pre-operations window ahead of the 2018-08-12 launch - and it is already cited in the processed record's own InformationURL list and in the Ephemeris record. No competing candidate paper. The later review (Raouafi et al. 2023, 10.1007/s11214-023-00952-4) was considered and set aside as a science review rather than a description paper.

Mission overview paper author order: backward scan found a sorted suffix of 12 names running from author 3 (Bale) to author 14 (Szabo), with the Velli-to-Bale step breaking alphabetical order. Classification: partially alphabetized, deliberate prefix = Fox, Velli (2 authors). Fox and Velli therefore take position-based Strong evidence and nobody else does. In particular the prefix was NOT padded out to five names from the alphabetized remainder - Bale, Decker and Driesman sit at positions 3, 4 and 5 by accident of the alphabet. Bale, Decker, Howard, Kasper, McComas, Raouafi and Szabo are all included, but each via an independent source (instrument PI listing, mission team page, or Instrument-record Contacts), never via their position in this list.

FIELDS paper author order (Bale et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-016-0244-5, 84 authors): the list is alphabetized by family name from author 10 (Andre) to the end, with two isolated single-name anomalies (Parker before Pankow at 66-67, Yehle before Werthimer at 82-83). A strict backward scan stops at those anomalies and would classify the list as not alphabetized; reading the anomalies as typographical gives a deliberate prefix of 9 (Bale, Goetz, Harvey, Turin, Bonnell, Dudok de Wit, Ergun, MacDowall, Pulupa). Both readings award Strong evidence to the same three people - Bale, Goetz, Harvey - so the ambiguity does not change the outcome. Prefix positions 4 and 5 (Turin, Bonnell) are recorded as excluded instrument-team depth; prefix positions 6-9 and the entire alphabetized remainder carry no position-based evidence and were not enumerated.

IS⊙IS paper author order (McComas et al. 2014, 10.1007/s11214-014-0059-1, 51 authors): authors 2-51 are cleanly alphabetized by family name, and McComas heads the list out of alphabetical order. Classification: partially alphabetized, prefix = 1 author. Only McComas takes position-based evidence; the prefix was not padded from the alphabetized remainder, so no other IS⊙IS author is a candidate on position. Eric Christian, at position 10 in the remainder, is included on the strength of his DeputyPI listing in the Instrument record instead.

SWEAP paper author order (Kasper et al. 2015, 10.1007/s11214-015-0206-3, 79 authors): authors 2-79 are alphabetized by family name with three isolated single-name anomalies (Gauron before Gates, McFadden before Marchant, Messina before Mercer), and Kasper heads the list out of alphabetical order. Reading the anomalies as typographical gives a deliberate prefix of 1 - Kasper alone. A strict backward scan would instead cut the sorted suffix at author 58 and treat authors 2 and 3 (Abiad, Austin) as prefix leads, which is plainly an artefact of the alphabet; the conservative reading was taken, so only Kasper earns position-based evidence. Michael Stevens, at position 69 in the remainder, is included because the mission team page names him the current SWEAP PI.

WISPR paper author order (Vourlidas et al. 2015, 10.1007/s11214-014-0114-y, 27 authors): the backward scan finds no sorted suffix of five or more - the list is grouped by institution, not alphabetized - so author order signals contribution. Positions 1-3 (Vourlidas, Howard, Plunkett) take Strong evidence; positions 4 and 5 (Korendyke, Thernisien) are recorded as excluded instrument-team depth; Mark Linton at position 11 gets no position-based evidence and is included instead on the mission team page's PI listing.

Two generations of instrument PI are present and the sources split cleanly by date. The founding PIs are Bale (FIELDS), McComas (IS⊙IS), Kasper (SWEAP) and Howard (WISPR) - this is what the SPASE Instrument records, NASA's instruments page, and the 2022 SPDF/CDAWeb readme all say. The 2026 JHU/APL mission team page keeps Bale and McComas but names Michael Stevens for SWEAP and Mark Linton for WISPR. Kasper and Howard are therefore recorded as FormerPI of their suites and Stevens and Linton as the sitting InstrumentLeads. Curators should note that the SWEAP and WISPR Instrument records (and all five of their sub-instrument records) are out of date on this point.

Discrepancy in the Observatory record's own Contacts: Nour Raouafi is listed with the role PrincipalInvestigator, but no source outside SPASE gives him that title - the JHU/APL mission team page names him Project Scientist, and Parker Solar Probe, as a strategic APL-led mission, has no mission-level science PI. ProjectScientist is what this run records for him. Nicola Fox, listed as ProjectScientist in the record, held that post during development and launch but is no longer on the mission team page, having moved to NASA Headquarters; her project-scientist role is kept but should be read as historical. Robert Decker is listed only as Scientist, which is not an author-qualifying role, yet the mission team page names him Deputy Project Scientist - he is included on that basis, not on the record's Contacts entry.

The JHU/APL mission team page contains a duplicated Project Scientist line, the second of which misspells the surname as 'Nour Rawafi'. This is the same person as Nour Raouafi and no separate candidate was created.

Person record duplicate to resolve downstream: the SWEAP PI exists twice in the registry, as spase://SMWG/Person/Michael.L.Stevens and spase://SMWG/Person/Michael.Louis.Stevens, both with PersonName 'Michael Louis Stevens' and the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics as organisation (the Michael.Louis.Stevens record additionally carries the email mstevens@cfa.harvard.edu). Michael.L.Stevens is cited above as the conventional First.Initial.Last form; a curator should merge them.

Missing Person records confirmed against the published registry, not just the local clone: Marco Velli and Arik Posner both return HTTP 404 at spase-metadata.org, as do Clarence M. Korendyke, Paul Turin, Andrew Driesman, David Lario and James Kinnison. Marco Velli is the most significant gap - he is the mission's Observatory Scientist and the second author of the overview paper, and needs a Person record before he can be cited.

Two mission-level titles have no counterpart in the SPASE role enumeration and so appear as Author only: Marco Velli's 'Observatory Scientist' and Adam Szabo's 'Mission Scientist'. Robert Decker's 'Deputy Project Scientist' was mapped to ProjectScientist with the deputy status stated in the role source, since SPASE has no deputy-project-scientist role.

No CMAD was located despite Parker Solar Probe being an operating, NASA-funded mission for which one is expected; see the cmad object for the three search strategies tried. Current-team evidence came from the 2026 JHU/APL mission team page instead, which is what surfaced the SWEAP and WISPR PI changes.

Instrument coverage is complete at suite level - all four suites named by every external source have SPASE Instrument records - but the sub-instrument tree has three structural gaps worth a curator's attention: IS⊙IS/EPI-Hi and FIELDS/RFS are each registered only through their component telescopes and receivers with no record of their own, and the FIELDS Time Domain Sampler sits at FIELDS/FIELDS2/TDS behind an intermediate 'FIELDS2' directory that has no record and does not correspond to any real instrument.

All twenty sub-instrument records were read. Every one carries exactly three Contacts - its suite PI as PrincipalInvestigator, Nicola J. Fox as ProjectScientist, and Lee Frost Bargatze as MetadataContact - so the deep tree yielded no people beyond those already captured at suite level. The sub-instrument teams themselves are deferred to pending_instrument_runs, per the Observatory-level scoping of this run.

This run took each suite's leads only - the Instrument record's qualifying-role contacts plus positions 1-3 of the suite description paper. Suite-paper authors at position 4 and beyond are instrument-team depth and belong to that Instrument record's own finder run; the fourth and fifth authors of the FIELDS and WISPR papers are listed individually as excluded, while the IS⊙IS and SWEAP papers have single-author prefixes and so have no fourth or fifth to consider.
